sentences.text: Isisaurus was a medium-sized sauropod estimated to reach 18 meters in length and weigh 15 metric tons.
This dinosaur possessed a short, upright neck and unusually long forelimbs compared to other sauropods.
No skull, hindlimb, or foot bones have been found for Isisaurus.
A complete scapula measures 108 centimeters in length and 29 to 60 centimeters in width.
The humerus bone of Isisaurus measures 148 centimeters in length.
The name Isisaurus honors the Indian Statistical Institute and means 'Indian lizard'.
The occipital bone in the Dongargaon skull deviates from its condyle at an angle of 120 degrees.
The species was first described as Titanosaurus colberti by Jain and Bandyopadhyay in 1997.
Wilson and Upchurch established the genus Isisaurus in 2003.
The first Isisaurus fossil discovery was described in 1982 and cataloged as ISI R199.
A second Isisaurus specimen was found in the same quarry nearly 20 years after the first, and was described 15 years after that discovery.
The original skeletal material discovered between 1984 and 1986 was found in an associated and mostly articulated condition.
Fossilized fungi found in coprolites attributed to Isisaurus suggest it ate leaves from various tree species.
Fossilized titanosaur coprolites indicate that these dinosaurs ate soft plant tissues and avoided hard foods.
The presence of specific fungi in Isisaurus coprolites suggests the habitat had a tropical or subtropical climate.
Invertebrate fossils found with Isisaurus include snails, bivalves, and ostracods, with the latter being distinct in the mentioned basins.
The exact classification of Isisaurus within the titanosaurian clade has been a subject of controversy.
In 2001, Isisaurus was placed within the family Titanosauridae under the genus Titanosaurus.
Wilson's 2002 tree shows Isisaurus as a sister group to Saltasauridae.
In 2021, Isisaurus was identified as the sister taxon to Arackar.
Isisaurus belongs to the parent group Saltasauroidea.
All Indian sauropods belong to the Titanosauria clade.
Isisaurus fossils have been found in the Late Cretaceous Lameta Formation of India and the Pab Formation of Pakistan.
The holotype was discovered at Dongargaon Hill in the Maastrichtian Lameta Formation of India.
The hill is located at coordinates 20.212318N, 79.090709E, near Warora in the Chandrapur district of Maharashtra.
Isisaurus lived in the territory of modern India during the Maastrichtian stage, the final stage of the Cretaceous period.
Isisaurus lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian.
It is debated whether the positions assigned to these types within the clade are secure, as they could instead be basal types elsewhere in the clade.
